easy.def: To grab or catch quickly.
examples: I nabbed the last seat.
She nabbed the ball.
He nabbed a cookie.

more.def: To grab, catch or get something quickly.
examples: I nabbed the last seat on the bus.
She nabbed the ball before it rolled away.
He nabbed a cookie from the plate.

easy.def: A corn chip with melted cheese on it.
examples: I ate nachos.
The nachos have cheese.
We shared a plate of nachos.

more.def: A crisp corn chip that is topped with melted cheese and sometimes beans or other toppings.
examples: We shared a plate of nachos with cheese and beans.
Each nacho was covered with melted cheese.
He dipped the nacho into the salsa.

easy.def: To keep asking someone to do something.
examples: Mom had to nag me about my room.
Don't nag me.
The little kids nag all day.

more.def: To keep asking or complaining to someone about something until they get annoyed.
examples: My little brother nagged me all afternoon to play with him.
Mom had to nag us to clean our rooms.
Do not nag the teacher about homework.

easy.def: A thin metal pin that you hit with a hammer.
examples: Dad hit the nail.
A nail holds the board.
The nail is sharp.

more.def: A thin metal spike that is hit with a hammer to hold pieces of wood together.
examples: Dad hit the nail with a hammer.
A rusty nail was stuck in the board.
The picture hangs from a small nail.

easy.def: The hard part at the end of a finger.
examples: I cut my nails.
Her nail is long.
He bit his nail.

more.def: The hard, thin layer at the tip of a finger or toe.
examples: I need to cut my nails.
She painted her nails blue.
He broke a nail.

easy.def: The word a person or thing is called.
examples: My name is Sam.
What is your dog's name?
Write your name here.

more.def: A word or words that a person, animal, place, or thing is known by.
examples: The name of our town is Maple Hill.
She wrote her name at the top of the page.
What is the name of that bird?

easy.def: To choose what something will be called.
examples: We named the puppy Max.
I will name my fish Bubbles.
They named the baby Ava.

more.def: To choose what someone or something will be called, or to say what it is called.
examples: The class named the classroom turtle Shelly.
Can you name all seven days of the week?
The explorers named the river after their captain.

easy.def: Having no name.
examples: The nameless cat came in.
A nameless puppy sat there.
The nameless hero rode away.

more.def: Having no name, or not known by name.
examples: A nameless puppy wandered into the yard.
The story is about a nameless traveler who crossed the desert.
The nameless stream ran through the woods.

easy.def: Another name for a grandmother.
examples: My nana bakes cookies.
I visit Nana.
Nana read me a story.

more.def: A name some people use for their grandmother.
examples: My nana bakes cookies every Sunday.
I call my grandmother Nana, and she calls me her sweetheart.
Nana taught me how to knit a scarf.

easy.def: A person who looks after children in their home.
examples: The nanny picked up the kids.
Our nanny reads stories.
The nanny cooks lunch.

more.def: A woman who is paid to look after children in their home.
examples: The nanny took the kids to the park.
Our nanny reads to us every night.
The nanny made lunch for the children.

easy.def: A short sleep in the day.
examples: The baby takes a nap.
I had a nap.
The cat is taking a nap.

more.def: A short sleep, usually during the day.
examples: The baby takes a nap every afternoon.
I had a nap after lunch.
The cat took a nap in the sun.

easy.def: A paper or cloth for wiping your mouth.
examples: I wipe my mouth with a napkin.
The napkin is white.
Put a napkin on your lap.

more.def: A small piece of cloth or paper that you use at meals to wipe your hands and mouth.
examples: I wiped my mouth with a napkin.
The napkin was folded on the plate.
Put the napkin on your lap.

easy.def: To tell a story.
examples: I narrate the story.
She narrated the film.
He will narrate.

more.def: To tell a story or describe what is happening, often out loud.
examples: She narrated the film about penguins.
The teacher will narrate the play.
He narrated the story at bedtime.

easy.def: A person who tells a story.
examples: The narrator read the story.
The narrator has a nice voice.
A narrator tells the tale.

more.def: A person or voice that tells a story.
examples: The narrator read the story aloud.
The movie had a narrator with a deep voice.
The narrator told us what happened next.

easy.def: Not wide.
examples: The path is narrow.
The cat fit through the narrow gap.
We walked on a narrow bridge.

more.def: Small in width; not wide.
examples: The street was so narrow that only one car could pass.
The bridge is too narrow for trucks.
A narrow stream ran through the field.

easy.def: By only a very small amount.
examples: He narrowly missed the bus.
She narrowly won.
We narrowly saved the cup.

more.def: Only just, by a very small amount.
examples: The ball narrowly missed the window.
Our team narrowly won the game by one point.
We narrowly caught the train as the doors were closing.

easy.def: Having to do with the nose.
examples: She had a nasal voice.
A nasal spray.
The cold made her nasal.

more.def: Having to do with the nose, or sounding as if a person is talking through the nose.
examples: When I have a cold, my voice sounds nasal.
The doctor gave me a nasal spray to help me breathe.
The nasal passages carry air from your nose to your throat.

easy.def: Mean, or very bad to taste or smell.
examples: He said a nasty thing.
The medicine tasted nasty.
The weather was nasty.

more.def: Very unkind, or very unpleasant to see, smell or taste.
examples: He said a nasty thing to his sister.
The medicine had a nasty taste.
A nasty storm blew the tent down.

easy.def: A country and its people.
examples: The whole nation watched the game.
Many nations sent athletes to the games.
Our nation has a flag.

more.def: A country, together with the people who live in it and the government that leads it.
examples: The president spoke to the whole nation.
Nations from all over the world come to the Olympic Games.
The United Nations helps countries work together.

easy.def: Of a whole country.
examples: The national flag.
A national holiday.
The national park.

more.def: Of or belonging to a whole country.
examples: The national flag flew over the building.
Yellowstone is a national park.
Thanksgiving is a national holiday.

easy.def: The country you belong to.
examples: Her nationality is Brazilian.
What is your nationality?
They have different nationalities.

more.def: The fact of belonging to a particular country.
examples: Her nationality is Canadian.
Students of many nationalities attend our school.
He was born in Mexico, so his nationality is Mexican.

easy.def: Happening across a whole country.
examples: A nationwide contest began.
It was a nationwide sale.
The nationwide race ends today.

more.def: Happening or found across the whole country.
examples: The nationwide spelling contest had winners from every state.
A nationwide storm warning was sent out.
The singer began a nationwide tour of fifty cities.

easy.def: Belonging to a place by birth.
examples: A native plant grows here.
She is a native speaker.
Kangaroos are native to Australia.

more.def: Born in a place, or naturally found there.
examples: The scientist studied native plants of the desert.
She is a native of this town.
The oak is a native tree here.

easy.def: People who were born in a place.
examples: The natives of the island are friendly.
The natives sang a song.
The natives of Texas are proud.

more.def: People or animals that were born in a place, or that have always lived there.
examples: The natives of the village welcomed us to the festival.
Many of the natives of the island speak two languages.
Natives of the area know the best places to fish.

easy.def: From nature, not made by people.
examples: A lake is natural.
Wool is a natural fabric.
She has natural curls.

more.def: Found in nature and not made or changed by people.
examples: A lake is a natural body of water.
Cotton is a natural fiber.
The cave is a natural wonder.

easy.def: Normal or expected.
examples: It is natural to be shy.
It is natural to be tired.
That is a natural reaction.

more.def: Normal or what you would expect.
examples: It is natural to feel nervous on the first day of school.
It was natural for the puppy to chew things.
His shy answer was a natural reaction.

easy.def: A person who studies plants and animals.
examples: The naturalist studies birds.
A naturalist walked in the woods.
The naturalist took notes.

more.def: A person who studies plants and animals in nature.
examples: The naturalist led a walk to look for birds.
A naturalist spent years studying the rain forest.
The naturalist wrote a book about wild flowers.

easy.def: In the usual way, or as you would expect.
examples: Naturally, I was happy.
She naturally likes to sing.
He naturally cried.

more.def: As you would expect, or in a way that comes from nature without being forced.
examples: Naturally, the dog was excited to go for a walk.
Her hair curls naturally, so she never needs a curler.
The kids naturally ran to the swings when they got to the park.

easy.def: Plants, animals, and all outdoor things not made by people.
examples: We like to walk in nature.
Birds and trees are part of nature.
We take care of nature.

more.def: Everything in the world not made by people, such as plants, animals, weather, and land.
examples: Hiking is a great way to enjoy nature.
She likes to draw things she finds in nature.
The power of nature can be seen in a big storm.

easy.def: Not behaving well.
examples: The naughty puppy chewed my shoe.
Do not be naughty.
The naughty cat knocked over the vase.

more.def: Behaving badly, often in a way that is not very serious.
examples: The naughty twins hid the teacher's chalk.
The children were naughty and ran in the halls.
The naughty cat knocked the vase off the shelf.

easy.def: A sick feeling in your stomach.
examples: The ride gave me nausea.
I felt nausea.
Nausea went away.

more.def: A sick feeling in your stomach, as if you might throw up.
examples: The bumpy boat ride gave me a feeling of nausea.
She felt nausea after eating too much candy.
The nausea passed after she drank some water.

easy.def: Making you feel sick.
examples: The smell was nauseating.
A nauseating ride.
The nauseating taste.

more.def: Making you feel sick to your stomach.
examples: The smell of the rotten eggs was nauseating.
The spinning ride was nauseating.
The nauseating taste of the old milk made me gag.

easy.def: Feeling like you might throw up.
examples: The bumpy ride made me nauseous.
He felt nauseous.
I was nauseous on the boat.

more.def: Feeling sick to your stomach, as if you might throw up.
examples: The winding road made me feel nauseous.
She felt nauseous after riding the spinning ride three times.
The strong smell of the paint made him nauseous.

easy.def: A sea animal with a shell that curls round and round.
examples: A nautilus lives in the sea.
The nautilus has a shell.
I saw a nautilus shell.

more.def: A sea animal with a spiral shell that has many small rooms inside.
examples: The nautilus swims by pushing water out of its body.
A nautilus shell is divided into rooms like a spiral staircase.
The nautilus lives deep in the ocean.

easy.def: Having to do with the navy.
examples: A naval ship is in port.
A naval officer.
The naval base is big.

more.def: Having to do with a navy and its ships.
examples: A naval ship docked in the harbor.
The naval officer wore a white uniform.
The naval base was near the sea.

easy.def: The small round dip in the middle of your belly.
examples: A baby has a navel.
The navel is on your tummy.
The shirt came above her navel.

more.def: The small, round dent in the middle of the belly, also called the belly button.
examples: The navel is where a baby was joined to its mother before birth.
He pointed to his navel and giggled.
Everyone has a navel on the middle of the stomach.

easy.def: To find the way.
examples: I navigate with a map.
The captain navigated the ship.
She navigated the road.

more.def: To find your way from one place to another, using a map, a compass or other tools.
examples: The captain navigated the ship through the foggy sea using a compass.
Dad used a map to navigate through the unfamiliar city.
Can you navigate the maze without getting lost?

easy.def: Finding the way from one place to another.
examples: The ship uses navigation.
Navigation helps us find the way.
A navigation map.

more.def: The skill or the process of finding the way from one place to another, using maps, a compass or other tools.
examples: The captain used a compass for navigation at sea.
The car has a screen for navigation that shows the roads.
Sailors long ago used the stars for navigation.

easy.def: A person who finds the way for a ship or plane.
examples: The navigator read the map.
A navigator helps the ship.
The navigator found the way.

more.def: A person whose job is to find the right way for a ship, a plane or a car to travel, using maps and instruments.
examples: The navigator on the ship used a compass and a map to find the island.
Dad was the navigator on our road trip, reading the map aloud.
The pilot and navigator planned the route across the ocean.

easy.def: A country's ships and the people who sail them.
examples: My uncle is in the navy.
The navy has big ships.
A navy ship came into port.

more.def: The part of a country's armed forces that works on the sea, with its ships and sailors.
examples: The navy keeps ships in the harbor.
My grandfather served in the navy for four years.
A navy ship brought supplies to the island.

easy.def: A very dark blue color.
examples: She wore a navy coat.
The flag is red, white and navy.
I like navy blue.

more.def: A very dark blue color.
examples: The school uniform is navy and white.
The sky turned navy as night came.
He painted the door navy.

easy.def: No.
examples: The people said nay.
Nay, I will not go.
Yea or nay?

more.def: An old word for no.
examples: The people shouted nay to the king's plan.
Nay, I will not go with you.
In the old story, the knight answered, Nay.
